# Hollow libnpth.so stub — the npth endgame (#48)
date: 2026-09-26   product sha256 9966e296…

## Why (recap)
npth is the confirmed residual mallocng corruptor via a NON-HOOK path: its worker
thread runs autonomous heap monitoring that writes Bionic-layout metadata over musl
mallocng (final-r5, npth-worker, autonomous 17.5s, engines idle). It is a repeat
multi-path offender (#46-3 thread walk, #48 inline hooks, r5 sigaction, now non-hook
heap). Point-patching one path at a time is whack-a-mole; replace the whole library.

## The stub (stub/libnpth_stub.c, generated by scripts/gen_npth_stub.py)
A hollow libnpth.so whose JNI_OnLoad:
  - registers every app-facing npth native as a typed-safe no-op, and
  - SPAWNS NOTHING (no worker/monitor thread) — the autonomous corruptor is gone —
  - installs no hook, calls no sigaction, does no heap monitoring, then returns
    JNI_VERSION_1_6.
So npth loads and its Java layer sees success, but the library does nothing: every
corruption path (hooks, sigaction, non-hook autonomous heap) is gone at the source
and cannot regress. The westlake recorder (out-crash42) already captures crashes.

The 81 natives need only 7 no-op C functions (one per return type): a JNI native
ignores its args, so on aarch64 a (JNIEnv*, jclass) fn registered for any signature
is safe (extra args sit in x2+ unread, caller-cleaned). RegisterNatives validates
the signature STRING against the Java method, not the C fn. Return defaults are
JNI primitives (no unbox -> no metasec-style NPE): void->return, boolean->JNI_FALSE,
int->0, long->0, String->"" (NewStringUTF), String[]->empty, object->NULL.

## App-facing ABI coverage — CONFIRMED complete (no UnsatisfiedLinkError)
Export surface: JNI_OnLoad only. Reverse-DT_NEEDED: none.
Registered = all 81 app npth natives across the 2 classes the app declares:
  com.bytedance.crash.jni.NativeBridge   71
  com.bytedance.apm.profiler.Profiler    10
assert_npth_hollow_48.sh checks every name from evidence/npth-app-abi-48.txt is in
the stub -> "all 81 app npth natives registered (no ULE)". If npth ever registered a
native the app does NOT declare, that is harmless (extra registration); if the app
declared one the stub misses, the assertion FAILS -> caught before board.

## Product (NOT deployed — board is codex-2's)
  gen:   scripts/gen_npth_stub.py evidence/npth-app-abi-48.txt stub/libnpth_stub.c
  build: stub/build_npth_stub.sh  (OH clang + JDK jni.h, -soname libnpth.so, -fvisibility=hidden)
  sha256: 9966e2966057c4d7d31f81232decf58da046898b9a2be900df675d44d016a107
  SONAME libnpth.so; exports JNI_OnLoad only; NEEDED only libc.so; 0 undefined
  non-libc symbols; no pthread_create / bytehook / shadowhook / sigaction imports.

## assert_npth_hollow_48.sh — PASS (8/8)
SONAME, JNI_OnLoad export, all 81 natives registered, both FindClass classes present,
hollow (NEEDED ⊆ {libc}), no worker-spawn/hook/sigaction imports, valid ELF.

## Board config for codex-2 (warm 5 rounds)
  shim 85c789f4 (baseline) + libnpth = HOLLOW STUB 9966e296 (replaces 7639af00)
  + memsponge 2f066332 + monitorcollector f3918bdc + sysopt c92d0ea5 (kept as
    protection so no other hooker re-corrupts).
Expect: npth-worker no longer exists (nothing spawned) so no autonomous mallocng
corruption; warm 5/5 with feed + article, SIG11=0. If a new source appears, it is
outside npth. jato patch (all 26 sites deref-safe) is ready if r4 still shows it.
